extracted.intended_audience: authors and peer reviewers of academic manuscripts (especially systematic reviews) and scholarly-publishing stakeholders interested in open peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or preparing a systematic review manuscript about open peer review: assess clarity of objectives, methods transparency, validity of claims, definitions/terminology, figures, and whether conclusions are supported by evidence. Also includes assigning a reviewer status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer status (decision categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alongside their report, reviewers assign a status to the article: Approved; Approved with reservations; Not approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved: The paper is scientifically sound in its current form and only minor, if any, improvements are suggested. Approved with reservations: A number of small changes, sometimes more significant revisions are required to address specific details and improve the paper's academic merit. Not approved: Fundamental flaws in the paper seriously undermine the findings and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of rationale and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the rationale for, and objectives of, the Systematic Review clearly stated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer expects a clear statement of why the review was done and what it aims to achieve; in this report the answer given is 'Yes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods transparency and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Are sufficient details of the methods and analysis provided to allow replication by others?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full details of the literature search, inclusion/exclusion criteria, data extraction and analytic procedures; identify who carried out specific searches (e.g., clarify any role attributed to projects like OpenAIRE). Reviewer marked this as 'Yes' after clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of statistical analysis and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the statistical analysis and its interpretation appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether quantitative claims/statistical descriptions are correct and supported; when not applicable, mark accordingly (the reviewer marked 'Not applicable' for this paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of conclusions by results
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the conclusions drawn adequately supported by the results presented in the review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions should follow from the data; reviewers should point out weak or overstated conclusions and ask for strengthening or qualification (the reviewer noted conclusions were correct but 'weak' and suggested expanding points about growth of interest and core/periphery distinctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear definitions and early placement of key terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Define core terms (e.g., Open Identities, Open Reports, open pre-review manuscripts/open preprints, open platforms) and present brief definitions close to where the schema or taxonomy is introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer criticised listing seven types of openness without definitions and recommended inserting definitions earlier; author added definitions as suggested. Definitions help readers avoid misapprehension about terms and reduce ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology accuracy and consistent usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use precise, non-misleading terminology (e.g., avoid calling something a 'platform' if it is a peer-review service; avoid ambiguous words like 'posting' that can be misread).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer pointed out that terms like 'open platforms' and 'open pre-review manuscripts' could be misconstrued; recommended reconsidering naming and clarifying scope (author amended wording e.g., 'Open platforms (“decoupled review”)'). Also advised choosing singular vs. royal 'we' consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overclaiming or misuse of technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use technical terms (e.g., 'power law') imprecisely or overstate the degree of generality (e.g., claiming a 'unified' definition when evidence shows multiple configurations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer recommended replacing 'power-law distribution' with a more cautious description ('a couple of very common configurations and a lot of rarer ones'); author changed text accordingly. Avoid claiming a 'unified' definition if contested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and sourcing for claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive claims (for example that PubPeer has been 'a major influence') should be backed by evidence or the language should be weakened to reflect uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer questioned evidence for some claims; author weakened wording to 'An important platform ... has been the independent platform PubPeer' to reduce overstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make core vs peripheral findings explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: When data suggest certain features are central (e.g., Open Identities/Open Reports) and others peripheral, make that core/periphery distinction explicit in conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer noted that 110/122 references mentioned 'Open Identities' and 72 mentioned 'Open Reports' and suggested emphasizing these as core elements; author extended and strengthened conclusions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify provenance of searches and data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state who carried out literature searches and how different searches (e.g., OpenAIRE vs author) were used, to avoid confusion over data provenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer noted apparent multiple literature surveys and asked for clarification; author clarified that the literature review was done by the main author as part of OpenAIRE and edited text to first person for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure and metric clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures and their metrics must be clearly labelled and explained (e.g., specify whether a chart shows number of articles, number of distinct definitions, targets of OPR mentions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer asked what the metric in Figure 4 represented; author clarified in text which targets (journal articles, data, grant proposals) were counted and how percentages were computed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address potential conflicts and implications of identity policies
rubrics_metrics.description: When discussing open identity review, discuss how revealing reviewer identities affects conflicts of interest and scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer suggested noting that open identity review in medicine makes conflicts of interest more apparent and subject to scrutiny; author added text quoting reviewer and addressing the point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and discuss alternative models and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention relevant alternative practices (e.g., publishers that publish reviewer names only upon acceptance) and discuss their trade-offs (e.g., risk of self-censorship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer recommended noting Frontiers' approach and that publishing reviewer names only after acceptance may avoid self-censorship; authors should acknowledge such variations and their implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and responsiveness in revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond constructively to reviewer comments, correct editorial issues (typos, awkward phrasing), and be willing to adjust wording or structure (e.g., change 'Unaccountability' to 'Lack of accountability').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer made detailed textual suggestions (word choice, sentence structure, moving definitions). The author addressed many such points in revision and explicitly noted changes in the author response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and reviewers should disclose competing interests relevant to the manuscript and review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing interests are reported on the page (e.g., reviewer declared consultancy for Frontiers Media; other reviewers declared no competing interests). Ensure transparency by disclosing such relationships.
